exam.title: CPP C++ Certified Professional Programmer
exam.study_prerequisites: CPA is recommended. Practice container selection and invalidation, half-open iterator ranges, algorithm preconditions and returned iterators, comparator/predicate contracts, remove/unique idioms, sorted merge/set operations, function objects, stream formatting state and function/class templates. The public block counts and weights are internally inconsistent, and the aligned course still labels CPP-22-01; use the active CPP-22-02 objectives without normalizing the published figures.

review.notes: Every named CPP-22-02 container, adapter, iterator, algorithm, function-object, stream-formatting and template objective is mapped with precondition/result/invalidation reasoning, three scenarios, ten labs and 30 original checks. The guide does not normalize the official internal inconsistency: the page says 40 questions while block counts total 32 and displayed weights total 107%. It also flags legacy ptr_fun and the aligned course's stale CPP-22-01 label. A broken provisional Pluralsight URL was rejected and replaced with the verified active C++ path before publication. O'Reilly and Udemy are automation-blocked. No recalled/live item, answer dump or copied course question is used. September 29 CPE source-health refresh updated shared-link counts only; this guide content and review date were not re-reviewed.

findings.title: Provider arithmetic and adapter scope need explicit interpretation
findings.evidence: The 34 objectives coexist with 107%weights/32 block items versus 40 questions, and adapter traversal wording.
findings.recommendation: Preserve published values, map everyobjective, explain the lack of publicadapteriterators and prioritize numbered objectives over the Heap title.
findings.resolution: Preserve published values, map everyobjective, explain the lack of publicadapteriterators and prioritize numbered objectives over the Heap title.

findings.title: Non-modifying chapter label obscures for_each mutation
findings.evidence: Serial for_each may modify elements and returns its callable; predicates have different requirements.
findings.recommendation: Correct the explanation and execute mutable, returned-state and reference-wrapper examples.
findings.resolution: Correct the explanation and execute mutable, returned-state and reference-wrapper examples.

findings.title: Capacity, invalidation and equivalence need concrete cases
findings.evidence: Reserve does not create output elements, deque end insertion preserves references but invalidates iterators, and ordered keys use comparison equivalence.
findings.recommendation: Add operation-specific contracts and execute all ten named container/adaptor families without stale access.
findings.resolution: Add operation-specific contracts and execute all ten named container/adaptor families without stale access.

findings.title: Algorithm boundaries and multiplicities are underspecified
findings.evidence: Empty needles, paired mismatch ends, allowed copy overlap, comparator equivalence transitivity and duplicate counts affect correctness.
findings.recommendation: Supply guarded serial cases, reject invalid preconditions before calls, and verify returned boundaries and sorted-set multiplicities.
findings.resolution: Supply guarded serial cases, reject invalid preconditions before calls, and verify returned boundaries and sorted-set multiplicities.

findings.title: Stream formatting description omits important state distinctions
findings.evidence: Noshowpoint does not cancel fixed precision; masked setf differs from ORing flags, and pending width can belong to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Execute exact strings, four-field restoration through exceptions, EOF recovery and injected output failure without clearing the error.
findings.resolution: Execute exact strings, four-field restoration through exceptions, EOF recovery and injected output failure without clearing the error.

findings.recommendation: Retain four observed probes separately from primary C++14/C++17 rules and use current callables in the main workbook.
findings.resolution: Retain four observed probes separately from primary C++14/C++17 rules and use current callables in the main workbook.
